youtube.title: Wells Fargo Bitcoin ETF Filing: What $2.35B Means | Crypto News
youtube.description:
Wells Fargo reported about 49.58 million shares of BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF (IBIT), valued near $2.35 billion on September 30, in a filing disclosed on November 16. It does not prove the bank bought that much Bitcoin with its own money.

Referral code: XOACPQFC

What happened:
• Wells Fargo's 13F listed about 49.58 million IBIT shares at the end of September.
• At the end of June, the figure was 24.4 million shares, so the count more than doubled.
• The value rose from roughly $812 million to about $2.35 billion.
• The filing can include assets managed for clients, not only the bank's own money.

Why it matters: Big banks and their clients now reach Bitcoin through familiar funds. But a September snapshot says nothing about buying or selling in November.

Source: NewsBTC, Nov 17, 2026 (citing a CoinDesk analysis)

FAQ
Did Wells Fargo buy $2.35 billion of Bitcoin?
Not exactly. It reported IBIT shares worth about $2.35 billion, and a 13F can include assets managed for customers.
What is IBIT?
It is BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, an ETF. Investors own fund shares, not Bitcoin in a wallet.
Does the filing show November trades?
No. It shows positions on September 30 only.

Updated: November 2026
